A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same conceptual work, The Impossibility of Fair LLMs. All 9 pages of v1 and 16 pages of v2 support comparison. Both end with references; neither contains appendices.

before.justification: v1 develops conceptual arguments and discusses findings attributed to cited research. It reports no original experiments, simulations, user studies, or data analyses.

after.justification: v2 remains a conceptual synthesis. Its evaluation proposals are future directions, and the Limitations section identifies empirical quantification as outstanding work. No original empirical outcomes are reported.

M1.justification: Neither version introduces an implemented algorithm or model. The new Approach section explains the conceptual analysis, while expanded suggestions for AI-assisted evaluation remain research proposals.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or tasks for original training or evaluation. Added discussion of multimodal systems and deployment contexts supplies conceptual examples.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates comparison methods against a proposed system. RLHF, DPO, Constitutional AI, and SELF-ALIGN remain examples discussed in the literature and future-research agenda.

E3.justification: Neither version reports an executed experimental protocol, data split, training budget, or evaluation configuration. v2's proposed evaluation approaches do not establish conducted experiments.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, robustness tests, or systematic supplementary empirical analyses. v2's Gemini controversy example illustrates its arguments using a cited account.

E5.justification: Repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, and statistical uncertainty estimation are absent from both versions.

E6.justification: Neither version supplies original empirical scores, rankings, or result entries. Added descriptions of external studies and conceptual implications do not constitute new results produced by this work.

T1.justification: Most definitions are recast in prose, but v2 omits v1 Definition 5's explicit conditional-independence criterion for calibration, retaining the shorter equal-precision description. Section 1 also extends the cited incompatibility claim to 'even to an approximation,' without explaining or deriving that stronger assertion. No new proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain: existing fairness frameworks cannot guarantee general-purpose LLM fairness, while contextual evaluation, developer responsibility, participation, and AI assistance offer productive directions. v2 foregrounds scalable evaluation, which v1 already advocates.

C2.justification: The new Limitations section materially qualifies the impossibility argument: it is not mathematically established, new frameworks might circumvent the barriers, and partial satisfaction remains unquantified. Sections 2–5 also expand interpretations concerning information asymmetry, ambiguous multimodal subjects, intersectionality, feedback amplification, regulation, and scalable evaluation through LLM judges and simulations.

D1.justification: Neither version provides study-specific implementation instructions, hyperparameters, hardware, or released code and data. Added references to existing tools do not document a new reproducible implementation.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning around evaluation science, practitioner experience, intersectionality, and scalable alignment, including Wallach et al. and Weidinger et al. (2025). It also changes supporting references for retained passages: Fairness of ChatGPT becomes the Phi-1.5 technical report, and Learning Gender-Neutral Word Embeddings becomes Adversarial Multiple Source Domain Adaptation. These are different works, not bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: v2 extensively rewrites the abstract and narrative, introduces an Approach section, merges v1's two main argument sections under Inherent challenges, and reorganizes the recommendations into three future-research sections. Definitions become inline prose, and separate Conclusion, Limitations, and Acknowledgments sections appear. D'Amour moves from the author list to acknowledgments.

P2.justification: The document is retypeset throughout, changing typography, column dimensions, spacing, title and affiliation layout, and bibliography presentation. v1's workshop running headers, copyright block, and keywords disappear; numbered citations become author–year citations. Neither version contains figures or tables.

improvement.justification: v2 improves scope disclosure through its explicit Limitations section and makes the research agenda more concrete and organized. However, retained examples acquire apparently mismatched supporting references, including the ChatGPT fairness and gender-neutral embedding passages. The introduction also strengthens an incompatibility claim to exclude approximation without explaining that extension. Clearer qualifications coexist with weakened evidential traceability and stronger unexplained wording, preventing a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
